propositions.text: The appellants are citizens of the DRC appealing the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claim for lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX1 and her daughters, XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXXX years old) and XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXXX years old),2 citizens of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), are appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rendered on February 3, 2017, rejecting their claim for refugee protection for lack of credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants from the DRC appeal the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claim for lack of credibility, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: The principal appellant was designated representative of her minor daughters by the RPD, designation ended when one daughter reached majority.
propositions.quote: The principal appellant was appointed by the RPD as the designated representative of her two (2) daughters, who were minors at the time.3 In accordance with the Refugee Appeal Division Rules,4 this representative is deemed to have been designated by the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD). However, given that XXXX reached the age of majority during the case, this designation ended on May 9, 2017.5

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal appellant was designated representative of her minor daughters, ending when one daughter reached majority.

propositions.text: The appellants did not submit new evidence or request a hearing for the appeal.
propositions.quote: The appellants did not submit any new evidence in support of their appeal and are not requesting a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes appellants submitted no new evidence and do not request a hearing.

propositions.text: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Minister did not intervene in the appeal.

propositions.text: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's determination that appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the determination of the RPD, namely, that the appellants are neither "Convention refugees" nor "persons in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's decision that appellants are not refugees or persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appellants allege fear of persecution due to spouse/father's political opinion and their status as vulnerable women.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege a fear of persecution by reason of the real or imputed political opinion of their spouse/father and because, as women, they are members of a vulnerable social group.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants allege fear of persecution due to spouse/father's political opinion and their vulnerability as women.

propositions.text: The spouse/father worked on a special project from 2013 to 2015 and was replaced after the appointing minister fell out of favour.
propositions.quote: The spouse/father allegedly worked on a special project, XXXX XXXX, from 2013 to 2015. As the minister who had appointed him had fallen out of favour with the party in power, he was allegedly replaced.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants say the spouse/father worked on a project from 2013-2015 and was replaced after the minister fell out of favour.

propositions.text: Four armed soldiers came to their home at night in 2015, robbed the spouse/father, and threatened to return if unsatisfied.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege that during the night of XXXX XXXX to XXXX, 2015, four (4) armed soldiers showed up at their home looking for information about the XXXX XXXX project; they robbed the spouse/father, taking his computers and work documents. They allegedly promised to come back if they were not satisfied.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants allege armed soldiers robbed the spouse/father in 2015 and threatened to return.

propositions.text: A complaint was filed the day after the first incident.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege that a complaint was filed the next day.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants say a complaint was filed the day after the first incident.

propositions.text: A second incident in 2016 involved soldiers and civilians invading the home, humiliating the principal appellant, threatening the family, and taking belongings.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege that a second incident occurred on XXXX XXXX, 2016, more than a year later. That time, six (6) men showed up during the night-four (4) soldiers and two (2) civilians. Four (4) of them stayed with the spouse/father in the bedroom, while the other two (2) went into the living room with the principal appellant and the children. She was allegedly humiliated in front of her children. The soldiers touched her all over her body, pointed a weapon at her head, and threatened to kill her, her children and her husband. She stated that she was not raped because the other soldiers objected after the husband paid them $600. They left, taking belongings with them and threatening to keep coming back because they were looking for important XXXX XXXX project documents.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants allege a 2016 home invasion with threats, humiliation, and theft involving soldiers and civilians.

propositions.text: A second complaint was filed the day after the second incident.
propositions.quote: The next day, a second complaint was allegedly filed.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants say a second complaint was filed after the second incident.

propositions.text: The appellants left the DRC in June 2016 to visit family in Canada; the spouse/father joined them a month later.
propositions.quote: The appellants left the DRC on June 27, 2016, to visit another of the family's children who is studying in Canada. They arrived here the next day. The spouse/father came to join them a month later.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants left the DRC in June 2016 to visit family in Canada; spouse/father joined later.

propositions.text: The family planned to return to the DRC together but the principal appellant stayed in Canada; the spouse/father lives in the DRC now.
propositions.quote: The family was supposed to return to the DRC together on XXXX XXXX, 2016, but the principal appellant decided to stay in Canada with her daughters. The couple's relationship had allegedly been strained since the second incident. The spouse/father apparently left and is living in the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: The family planned to return to DRC but principal appellant stayed; spouse/father now lives in DRC.

propositions.text: They filed their refugee claim on September 28, 2016.
propositions.quote: They filed their claim for refugee protection on September 28, 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants filed their refugee claim on September 28, 2016.

propositions.text: IRPA does not specify the standard of intervention for RAD reviewing RPD decisions; case law defines it.
propositions.quote: The IRPA does not set out the standard of intervention to be applied by the RAD when reviewing RPD decisions. This standard has been defined by the case law.

paragraphs.summary: The court states IRPA lacks a standard of intervention for RAD review; case law defines it.

propositions.text: Huruglica says RAD must analyze record to see if RPD erred; correctness standard applies to fact findings without credibility issues.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica,16 the Federal Court of Appeal ruled that the RAD must carry out its own analysis of the record to determine whether, as submitted by the appellant, the RPD erred. With respect to findings of fact (and mixed fact and law) that raised no issue of credibility of oral evidence, the RAD is to review RPD decisions applying the correctness standard.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Huruglica: RAD reviews RPD decisions for errors, applying correctness standard if no credibility issues.

propositions.text: If credibility issues arise and RPD had advantage, RAD applies modified reasonableness standard with explanation.
propositions.quote: In the case of findings of fact that do raise issues of credibility of oral evidence, the three-member RAD panel18 determined that if the RPD enjoyed a meaningful advantage, the RAD will explain how the RPD enjoyed such an advantage, if applicable, and may apply the standard of reasonableness, modified to apply to the RAD context.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites that with credibility issues and RPD advantage, RAD applies modified reasonableness standard with explanation.

propositions.text: The court finds RPD had undeniable advantage from observing appellants' demeanour and will apply modified reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: In this situation, having listened to the full recording of the hearing, I have no hesitation in concluding that deference is warranted, given the undeniable advantage enjoyed by the RPD, which had the opportunity to observe the appellants and their demeanour at the hearing during any silences and hesitations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD had advantage observing appellants and applies modified reasonableness standard.

propositions.text: The RPD accepted spouse/father worked on the project but doubted other alleged facts, finding them unproven on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The RPD accepted that the spouse/father had indeed worked for the XXXX XXXX project, but it was not satisfied that the rest of the alleged facts had been established. It was of the opinion that the various points combined had a sufficiently negative impact on the essential elements in question to find that they had not been established on a balance of probabilities.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD accepted spouse/father's work but found other facts unproven on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: The RPD found multiple contradictions and omissions undermining credibility of the appellants' claims.
propositions.quote: According to the RPD, the following points are problematic: * The major contradiction with respect to the date on which the complaint regarding the first home invasion was allegedly filed. * The omission in the first complaint of the allegation that the criminals wanted to obtain information regarding the XXXX XXXX project. * Their alleged behaviour following the first complaint raised concerns as to the truth of the alleged incident (incident of XXXX XXXX, 2015). * The implausibility of the connections made by the principal appellant between the second home invasion and the XXXX XXXX project (recognizing voices, statements not reported in the Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), demeanour during her testimony). * The contradictions between the principal appellant's testimony and that of her daughters, as well as between her daughters' testimony and their BOC Form regarding whether the criminals had been masked during the second incident. * The contradiction between the principal appellant's testimony and that of her daughters regarding steps taken to protect themselves following the second alleged home invasion (whether or not they returned home). * The failure to report the connection between the second home invasion and the XXXX XXXX project in the second complaint. * The contradiction between the principal appellant's testimony and the email of XXXX XXXX, 2016, regarding when she found out that there had allegedly been two more night-time visits to their home in the DRC. With regard to this same documentary evidence, the RPD noted that the principal appellant had a great deal of difficulty testifying and giving explanations. It was not satisfied with the explanations provided to explain the delay between when the new incidents occurred (XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, 2016) and when the principal appellant was allegedly informed of them by email. It noted that the principal appellant did not know whether the criminals had come back once or several times, although the email indicates two new visits and she stated that she had spoken to her husband about the email. Lastly, the RPD noted that it took the principal appellant more than two (2) months to communicate this relevant information to her counsel and, ultimately, to the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found many contradictions and omissions undermining appellants' credibility.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's laboured and contradictory testimony on intentions and spouse exchanges undermined credibility
propositions.quote: The appellant's laboured and contradictory testimony regarding her intentions upon leaving the country, her decision to remain in Canada and her exchanges with her spouse.

propositions.text: RPD noted spouse's decision to return to DRC despite visa to Canada reinforced lack of credibility
propositions.quote: Her spouse's decision to return to the DRC and stay there despite having a visa permitting him to return to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant's contradictory testimony and spouse's return to DRC despite visa collectively undermined credibility.

propositions.text: RPD concluded evidence did not establish spouse was at risk of persecution
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the evidence did not establish that her spouse was at risk of persecution.

propositions.text: RPD found appellants did not establish serious possibility of persecution due to social group or imputed political opinion under section 96 IRPA
propositions.quote: It follows that the appellants did not establish that there is a serious possibility that they would be persecuted by reason of their membership in the particular social group of [translation] "spouse's family members" or by reason of an imputed political opinion (section 96, IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The RPD concluded the appellants failed to prove serious risk of persecution of spouse or family under section 96 IRPA.

propositions.text: RPD analyzed claim under section 97 IRPA about personal danger of torture or risk not generally faced in DRC
propositions.quote: The RPD also analyzed their claim under section 97 of the IRPA, namely, whether they would be subjected personally to a danger of torture or to a risk not generally faced by other individuals in the DRC.

propositions.text: RPD concluded appellants did not discharge burden of proof under section 97 IRPA
propositions.quote: For a number of reasons, the RPD concluded that they had not discharged their burden of proof.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellants failed to prove personal risk of torture or unique risk under section 97 IRPA.

propositions.text: Appellants submit RPD erred in law by not considering all evidence on record
propositions.quote: Essentially, the appellants submit that the RPD decision is wrong in law because it did not take into consideration all of the evidence on the record.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD erred legally by failing to consider all evidence.

propositions.text: Appellants say RPD misinterpreted or improperly assessed multiple elements including appellant's decision to remain in Canada, complaint date, home invasion connections, contradictions about criminals' identities, email evidence, and credibility
propositions.quote: They submit that the following elements were misinterpreted or improperly assessed: * The appellant's decision not to return to the DRC with her spouse on XXXX XXXX, 2016, and to remain in Canada with her daughters. * The date of the first complaint. * The failure to mention a connection between the first home invasion and the XXXX XXXX project. * The contradiction regarding the return to their home, following the home invasion incident. * The statement that it is implausible that the appellant recognized the criminals' voices. * The contradiction regarding whether or not the criminals were masked at the time of the second home invasion. * The email of XXXX XXXX, 2016. * The return to their home following the second incident. * The fact that they are not credible is not a determinative factor, and they should nevertheless be considered refugees if the subjective and objective components are met.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD misinterpreted or improperly assessed many evidentiary elements and credibility issues.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's testimony laboured, contradictory, and not candid regarding intentions and spouse exchanges
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the appellant's testimony was laboured and contradictory with regard to her intention to leave the country, her decision to remain in Canada and her exchanges with her spouse on these subjects.

propositions.text: RPD doubted spouse was in danger or living in hiding since he had valid visa and returned to work
propositions.quote: In addition, the RPD doubted that her spouse was in danger and that he had to live in hiding, as the appellant claimed, since he had a valid visa for Canada at the time and had returned to work at the Société nationale d'électricité (XXXX).

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's testimony contradictory and doubted spouse's danger claim due to valid visa and return to work.

propositions.text: Appellants argue panel misinterpreted their actions of remaining in Canada and spouse returning alone
propositions.quote: The appellants argue that the panel misinterpreted their actions (remaining in Canada and letting her spouse return to the DRC alone).

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue the panel misinterpreted their decision to stay in Canada while spouse returned alone.

propositions.text: Disagreement with RPD conclusion insufficient; appellants must identify evidence and errors to intervene
propositions.quote: Merely disagreeing with a conclusion of the RPD is not sufficient grounds for me to intervene. The onus is on the appellants to clearly identify in their memorandum references to evidence and the passages where the RPD allegedly erred.

propositions.text: Appellants did not specify how RPD misinterpreted decisions or cite evidence for contrary conclusion
propositions.quote: They do not state how the RPD misinterpreted their decisions and they make no reference to evidence upon which I could rely to draw a contrary conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellants must identify errors and evidence; they failed to do so regarding RPD misinterpretation.

propositions.text: Court satisfied RPD's points were based on evidence after hearing recording
propositions.quote: I am satisfied, after listening to the recording of the hearing, that each of the points raised and considered by the RPD in coming to this conclusion is based on the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court is satisfied RPD's conclusions were evidence-based after reviewing hearing recording.

propositions.text: Appellant stated she did not intend to stay in Canada and did not discuss plan with spouse
propositions.quote: I also note the appellant's statement that, when she came to Canada, she did not intend to stay here and that she did not discuss her plan to stay here with her spouse.

propositions.text: This inconsistency supports RPD's negative credibility finding
propositions.quote: In my opinion, this is not consistent with her allegations concerning her subjective fear. The RPD was therefore correct in concluding that this supported its negative finding regarding the principal appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: RPD weighed this factor as reinforcing but not determinative of credibility findings
propositions.quote: The RPD wisely weighed this and stated that this factor was not determinative on its own, but simply reinforced the findings already made.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's inconsistent statements support RPD's credibility finding, which was not solely determinative.

propositions.text: RPD noted three problematic aspects of evidence about first home invasion including complaint date
propositions.quote: The RPD noted three (3) different problematic aspects of the appellants' evidence regarding the first home invasion, including the date on which a complaint was filed regarding this incident.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD identified three problematic aspects of appellants' evidence on the first home invasion, including complaint date.

propositions.text: Appellant testified incident occurred night of XXXX to XXXX 2015, confirmed in BOC Form
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the appellant testified that the incident took place during the night of XXXX XXXX to XXXX, 2015, which confirmed what she had written in her BOC Form.

propositions.text: Appellant uncertain when complaint filed; RPD confronted her with complaint copy dated two days later
propositions.quote: Later during the hearing, she stated that she could not recall exactly when she went to the police to file a complaint. The RPD then read her previous statements to her, and she again confirmed that the date of the complaint was XXXX XXXX. The RPD confronted her with the fact that the copy of the complaint submitted into evidence was dated XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Appellant maintained complaint filed day after incident despite documentary evidence showing two days later; contradiction unexplained
propositions.quote: She maintained that she was certain that the complaint had been filed the day after the incident. The RPD was of the opinion that, although the difference was only one or two (2) days, this contradiction had not been explained.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant contradicted herself on complaint date, claiming next day filing despite evidence showing two days later.

propositions.text: Appellants argue panel failed to understand appellant was in shock and memory lapse was normal
propositions.quote: The appellants submit that the panel made no attempt to understand that the (principal) appellant was in shock after allegedly being assaulted and that it was normal for her not to remember the exact day the complaint was filed.

propositions.text: Appellants argue 'next day' could mean two days later due to shock, so misstatement not contradiction
propositions.quote: They submit a second argument: that, in the appellant's mind, the next day could just as easily have meant two days later, given that she was deeply shaken.

propositions.text: Appellants say reasonable person would see this as misstatement, not contradiction, given shock after assault
propositions.quote: According to the appellants, a reasonable person in the same circumstances would conclude that it was misstatement, not a contradiction, taking into account the fact that the appellant was in shock after being sexually assaulted.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue the panel failed to consider appellant's shock causing memory lapse, so date discrepancy is misstatement, not contradiction.

propositions.text: Court finds appellant contradicted herself and did not merely misspeak
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the principal appellant did contradict herself, and did not simply misspeak, as counsel for the appellants would have me believe.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant contradicted herself rather than merely misspeaking.

propositions.text: BOC Form and initial testimony state complaint filed next day
propositions.quote: First, I note that the BOC Form is clear with respect to when the complaint was filed-the next day. The appellant's initial testimony was also to that effect.

propositions.text: RPD clarified 'next day' meaning; appellant hesitated but agreed it was XXXX XXXX; later said she did not remember date
propositions.quote: Then, the RPD sought to clarify exactly what "the next day" meant for her. She replied "the day after the assault, the day after they visited us." The RPD again insisted, given that the alleged incident occurred during the night of XXXX XXXX to XXXX, and asked whether for her the next day meant XXXX XXXX. The RPD suggested "so, it was on XXXX XXXX?" and she hesitated at length before finally replying "I think so, yes." Then, she murmured "I don't remember the date anymore."

propositions.text: Confronted with complaint dated two days later, appellant said husband filed complaint next day
propositions.quote: After being confronted with the fact that the documentary evidence indicates that the complaint was filed on XXXX XXXX, two (2) days and two (2) nights later, she replied, "I myself know, I know that my husband filed the complaint the next day."

paragraphs.summary: The court details appellant's inconsistent testimony about complaint date and hesitation when confronted with documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Court rejects appellants' arguments for three reasons
propositions.quote: My analysis of the evidence leads me to reject the appellants' arguments for three (3) reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects appellants' arguments for three reasons.

propositions.text: Appellant's spontaneous reference was event sequence, not date; complaint date in evidence inconsistent with her testimony
propositions.quote: First, the appellant's spontaneous point of reference is not the date, but rather the sequence of events: she stated that one night the assault occurred and the next day the complaint was filed. In either scenario, as the RPD rightly suggested, this would mean that the complaint would have been filed on either XXXX XXXX or XXXX XXXX, but not on XXXX XXXX. Yet, the documentary evidence submitted by the appellants indicates that it was filed on XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's reference to sequence conflicts with documentary evidence on complaint date.

propositions.text: Appellant never testified 'next day' could mean two days later; no evidence supports that interpretation
propositions.quote: Second, contrary to what the appellants argue in their memorandum, at no time did the appellant testify that for her "the next day" could also mean two (2) days later. I therefore have no evidence to support such an interpretation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence appellant meant 'next day' to include two days later.

propositions.text: Appellant referred to 'assault' when explaining 'next day' but assault occurred during second home invasion, not first
propositions.quote: Third, when explaining what she meant by "the next day," the appellant spontaneously referred to "the assault." However, according to the evidence, the assault did not occur during the first home invasion incident, but rather during the second.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes appellant's reference to assault conflicts with evidence that assault occurred during second home invasion.

propositions.text: RPD thoroughly examined evidence and gave appellant opportunity to clarify contradiction; drew negative credibility inference
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the RPD thoroughly canvassed this aspect of the evidence and gave the appellant every opportunity to clarify this contradiction in her evidence. The RPD drew a negative inference as to her credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD properly examined evidence, allowed clarification, and drew negative credibility inference.

propositions.text: The RPD properly assessed all evidence on the connection between the first home invasion and the XXXX XXXX project.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the RPD properly assessed all of the evidence on this point.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD properly assessed evidence on the first home invasion's connection to the XXXX XXXX project.

propositions.text: The RPD found no mention of the connection in the complaint and found it unreasonable police or spouse would omit this key connection.
propositions.quote: The RPD found it unreasonable that, as the appellant suggested, the police would have failed to note this important connection, had they been informed of it.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no mention of the connection in the complaint and deemed it unreasonable police or spouse would omit it.

propositions.text: Appellants argue the mother did not file the complaint and could not know what husband told police; husband must have disclosed the detail but police did not note it.
propositions.quote: They argue that they are certain that the spouse/father would have disclosed this [translation] "detail" to the police and that the police must not have made note of it.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the mother did not file the complaint and husband disclosed the detail, but police failed to note it.

propositions.text: The court agrees with RPD that the appellants claim spouse signed an incomplete complaint omitting a key motive, which is not a mere detail.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that this is not a detail but a key aspect of this home invasion and the theft of the particular property that was taken.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the omitted motive is a key aspect, not a mere detail, of the home invasion complaint.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellant testified she accompanied spouse but he did all talking; she believed he explained reasons but could not confirm police noted it.
propositions.quote: The RPD patiently tried to verify whether the information had been given to the police.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant testified she accompanied spouse but he did all talking and she was unsure if police noted the reasons.

propositions.text: Appellant gave no explanation how spouse could ignore such an important aspect of the incident, especially threats to return.
propositions.quote: At no time did she provide an explanation for how her husband could have ignored such an important aspect of this first incident.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant gave no explanation how spouse could ignore the important aspect of threats to return.

propositions.text: Without the motive detail, the complaint recounts a random theft, not the appellants' circumstances.
propositions.quote: Without this detail, the complaint simply recounts a random theft, not the circumstances put forward by the appellants.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the complaint without motive detail recounts random theft, not appellants' circumstances.

propositions.text: The court agrees the RPD properly assessed the evidence regarding the contradiction about returning home after the invasion.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the RPD properly assessed the evidence. The contradiction regarding the return to their home following the home invasion

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the RPD properly assessed evidence about the contradiction on returning home after the invasion.

propositions.text: The RPD found that remaining at home and returning to Canada without claiming protection shows no steps to mitigate risks.
propositions.quote: The RPD was of the opinion that the fact that they remained at the home, stated that life went on and took a return trip to Canada (without claiming refugee protection) does not show that they took any steps to mitigate or eliminate the alleged risks.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found remaining at home and returning to Canada without claiming protection shows no risk mitigation steps.

propositions.text: Appellants allege RPD erred; their behaviour was consistent as thefts are common and they sought refuge with a friend temporarily.
propositions.quote: The appellants allege that the RPD erred in its analysis and that their behaviour was consistent because the appellant had explained that thefts are commonplace in the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants allege RPD erred; their behaviour was consistent given common thefts and temporary refuge with a friend.

propositions.text: Appellants misunderstood RPD's reference to first incident; they sought refuge with parents after second incident, not a friend after first.
propositions.quote: The appellants have misunderstood the RPD's statements, which explicitly refer to the first incident, as the subheading in its decision indicates.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellants misunderstood RPD; refuge was with parents after second incident, not a friend after first.

propositions.text: Appellants failed to persuade court that RPD erred; RPD's finding is correct.
propositions.quote: In the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the appellants have failed to persuade me that the RPD erred on this point.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellants failed to persuade that RPD erred; RPD's finding is correct.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's claim to recognize criminals' voices implausible due to omission and evasive testimony.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that her entire testimony on a key element of her story had a negative impact on the assessment of her testimony, given that it was implausible that she would remember the voices.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's claim to recognize criminals' voices implausible due to omission and evasive testimony.

propositions.text: Appellants criticize RPD for finding implausible that appellant remembered criminals' voices, arguing traumatic voices are unforgettable.
propositions.quote: The appellants criticize the RPD for concluding that it was implausible that she (the principal appellant) would be able to remember the criminals' voices.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants criticize RPD for finding it implausible appellant remembered criminals' voices, arguing traumatic voices are unforgettable.

propositions.text: Appellants do not challenge omission of voice recognition; omission undermines credibility and makes implausibility finding secondary.
propositions.quote: I note that the appellants are not challenging the omission noted by the RPD, namely, the appellant's failure to mention this means of identification.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes appellants do not challenge omission of voice recognition, which undermines credibility and makes implausibility finding secondary.

propositions.text: Court rejects appellants' argument; omission of voice recognition fact in BOC Form is significant regardless of plausibility.
propositions.quote: In the circumstances, I reject this argument because whether they are right or wrong does not change the fact that it should have been disclosed when she completed her BOC Form.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects appellants' argument; omission of voice recognition fact in BOC Form is significant regardless of plausibility.

propositions.text: RPD found children's testimony contradicted itself and mother regarding whether criminals were masked, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the children's testimony reinforced its doubts as to the credibility of their allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found children's testimony contradicted itself and mother on criminals being masked, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: Appellants criticize RPD for focusing on minor detail of whether criminals were masked, arguing even adults would struggle to recall.
propositions.quote: The appellants criticize the RPD for focusing on a minor detail and argue that it would be difficult even for an adult to accurately state whether the criminals had been masked or not.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants criticize RPD for focusing on minor detail of criminals being masked, arguing even adults would struggle to recall.

propositions.text: Court acknowledges testifying is stressful, especially for children aged 17 and 15 at time of events and hearing.
propositions.quote: I am mindful that testifying is stressful for any person claiming refugee protection, let alone a child.

paragraphs.summary: The court acknowledges testifying is stressful, especially for children aged 17 and 15 at time of events and hearing.

propositions.text: Court disagrees with appellants that difficulty describing faces in dark excuses contradictions about criminals being masked.
propositions.quote: However, what is at issue is not the accuracy of the description of the criminals' faces. Therefore, I disagree with the appellants' argument.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with appellants that difficulty describing faces excuses contradictions about criminals being masked.

propositions.text: Children did not testify uncertainty about seeing criminals' faces; speculation is insufficient, statements must be evidence-based
propositions.quote: The children did not testify that they were not sure whether they had seen the criminals' faces. One cannot simply put forward speculation: statements must be tied to the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds children did not express uncertainty about seeing criminals' faces and rejects speculation without evidence.

propositions.text: XXXX stated she saw faces of two men present
propositions.quote: XXXX stated that she had seen the faces of two (2) of the men who were there.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found XXXX saw faces of two men present.

propositions.text: XXXX testified she had nothing to add to sister's testimony and saw three or four men
propositions.quote: XXXX testified that she had nothing to add to her sister's testimony. She did not correct her sister's testimony. She stated, however, that she saw three (3) or four (4) men.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found XXXX saw three or four men and did not contradict sister's testimony.

propositions.text: Children were not talkative or spontaneous and could not describe criminals beyond men, black, unknown to them
propositions.quote: I note that they were not very talkative or spontaneous. They were unable to describe the criminals, even in general terms (young or old). They did not mention how they were dressed. Ultimately, the only information obtained by means of a series of questions increasingly led by the RPD was that they were men, they were black, and that the girls did not know them, would not recognize them and had seen their faces.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds children were uncommunicative and only described criminals as black men unknown to them.

propositions.text: Children contradicted mother and BOC Form; mother testified in daughters' absence and intervened when daughters' testimony differed
propositions.quote: They contradicted their mother and their BOC Form. The principal appellant testified in her daughters' absence, at her request and with the agreement of all. They did not hear the account given earlier by their mother. The RPD also noted that the girls looked to their mother for approval later during their testimony. Seeing that her daughters were providing information that differed from her testimony, the principal appellant intervened and the RPD had to reframe things to enable the children to say what they had to say.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds children contradicted mother and BOC Form; mother testified separately and intervened during daughters' testimony.

propositions.text: RPD correctly assessed children's credibility
propositions.quote: I find that the RPD correctly assessed the children's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD correctly assessed the children's credibility.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's email from spouse had no probative value for multiple reasons including contradictions and timing
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the email the appellant received from her spouse on XXXX XXXX, 2016, had no probative value for several reasons. First, because the appellant's testimony regarding the new incidents described in this email and when she learned of them was strained, hesitant and evasive. Second, because she contradicted herself regarding the content, as she stated that she had learned that these new incidents had occurred upon receiving the email, whereas in the email, her spouse states, [translation] "as I told you on the telephone." Third, because her spouse apparently waited until XXXX XXXX, 2016, to inform the appellant of incidents that occurred on XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX, 2016, although they were in contact with each other and he knew that the appellants had filed a claim for refugee protection. Fourth, because the appellant did not know whether the criminals had come more than once, although she stated that she had discussed the email, which indicates that there were two (2) incidents, with her spouse. Fifth, because the appellant did not report these new incidents until the hearing and allegedly forgot to disclose the information to her own counsel prior to the day before the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's spouse's email lacked probative value due to contradictions, timing, and late disclosure.

propositions.text: RPD considered the email an attempt to mislead the panel
propositions.quote: The RPD considered that this was an attempt to mislead the panel.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD considered the email an attempt to mislead the panel.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD erred by not considering rocky relationship explaining lack of communication
propositions.quote: The appellants argue that the RPD erred in its analysis. They acknowledge that there is a contradiction in the appellant's allegations concerning her statement that she had not heard from her spouse. However, they submit that the RPD failed to consider that the couple's relationship was rocky, since he had left in anger when the appellant told him that she did not intend to return to the DRC, which further explains the lack of communication.

propositions.text: Appellants argue email phrase does not prove spouse told appellant by telephone about criminals' return
propositions.quote: They add that the fact that the email states [translation] "as I told you on the telephone" does not prove that her spouse had told the appellant on the telephone that the criminals had returned.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD erred by ignoring rocky relationship and that email phrase does not prove telephone communication about criminals.

propositions.text: Court rejects appellants' first argument; RPD considered all allegations explaining difficult spouse situation
propositions.quote: I cannot accept the appellants' first argument, as the RPD explicitly considered all of the appellant's allegations to explain the difficult situation with her spouse-specifically, the incidents themselves, her decision not to return to her country and her suspicions that her husband was having an affair.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects appellants' first argument, finding RPD considered all relevant allegations about spouse situation.

propositions.text: Court rejects second argument; email indicates only that leaving house was not told by telephone
propositions.quote: I cannot accept the second argument either, as it would mean precisely the opposite of what is stated in the email. According to this email, the only information that was not communicated by telephone was the fact that these events had driven her spouse to leave the house. Indeed, the email states, [translation] "I did not tell you that this has driven me to leave the house. I am currently staying with cousin XXXX in Kimbangu."

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects appellants' second argument, interpreting email as showing only leaving house was not told by telephone.

propositions.text: RPD correctly assessed probative value of email evidence and found it has no probative value
propositions.quote: Ultimately, the RPD correctly assessed the probative value of this evidence. I agree with the RPD's conclusion that it has no probative value.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with RPD that the email evidence has no probative value.

propositions.text: RPD noted contradictions in appellants' evidence about steps after second home invasion; children contradicted mother and were hesitant
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that there was a contradiction in the appellants' evidence regarding what steps they took following the second home invasion, which allegedly occurred on XXXX XXXX, 2016. The children contradicted their mother's testimony and they were hesitant, looking to her to gauge her reaction. The RPD gave the appellant the opportunity to comment on her daughters' testimony, and she again gave an evasive and contradictory testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found contradictions and hesitancy in appellants' evidence about actions after second home invasion.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD misread facts; say children would not count days or recite them like a lesson
propositions.quote: The appellants state that the RPD misread and misinterpreted the facts. They argue that it would be absurd for the children to be able to count these days or recite them like a lesson.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD misread facts and that children would not count or recite days like a lesson.

propositions.text: Court disagrees with appellants' arguments
propositions.quote: I do not agree with the appellants' arguments.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with appellants' arguments about misreading facts.

propositions.text: RPD did not ask children how many days away but whether they returned home, assessing consistency of fear and behaviour
propositions.quote: The RPD did not ask the children how many days they spent away from their home. It wanted to know whether or not they had returned to the house. The RPD was assessing the consistency between their alleged subjective fear and their behaviour.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD assessed whether children returned home to evaluate consistency of fear and behaviour.

propositions.text: Recording shows contradictions: mother said returned home after few days; children said no return; mother later said children sometimes came and slept at home
propositions.quote: A review of the recording reveals, beyond a shadow of a doubt, the contradictions in this portion of the evidence: * The principal appellant initially testified that the day after the second home invasion, she took the children and went to stay with her parents for a few days. She stated that after a few days, [translation] "I returned home." * The children, on the other hand, testified that they had not returned home after XXXX XXXX. They allegedly stayed at the home of one of their mother's friends. * Their mother then commented on their testimony and stated that, [translation] "Sometimes the girls came there, sometimes they did not. They came to the house twice. To sleep, like that, they did not come." * Their mother then stated that, [translation] "Yes, they slept at home."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds contradictions in evidence about whether appellants returned home after second invasion.

propositions.text: RPD's finding that appellants did not credibly establish behaviour consistent with seriousness of situation is founded; lack of credibility not determinative if subjective and objective components met
propositions.quote: In the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the RPD's finding, that they had not credibly established that their behaviour was consistent with the seriousness of the situation alleged in their story, is founded. The appellants have not persuaded me otherwise. The fact that they are not credible is not a determinative factor and they should nevertheless be considered refugees if the subjective and objective components are met

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees RPD found appellants' behaviour not credibly consistent with situation seriousness but notes credibility is not determinative alone.

propositions.text: RPD concluded appellants did not establish past home invasion or future persecution risk based on social group membership
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the appellants had not established that they were the victims of a home invasion in their country in the past or that that they would face a serious possibility of persecution in the future by reason of their membership in the particular social group of [translation] "spouse's family members / imputed political opinion" or by reason of their membership in the particular social group of [translation] "women."

paragraphs.summary: The RPD concluded appellants failed to establish past home invasion or future persecution risk based on social group.

propositions.text: Appellants submit they must be considered refugees if subjective and objective components met, regardless of credibility
propositions.quote: The appellants submit that they must be considered refugees whether they are credible or not, as long as they meet the subjective and objective components for being granted refugee status.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue refugee status should be granted if subjective and objective components met, regardless of credibility.

propositions.text: Both subjective and objective components are necessary under section 96 of the Act for refugee status.
propositions.quote: According to the case law, it is true that both the subjective and objective components are necessary to satisfy the requirements of section 96 of the Act.

propositions.text: If subjective fear is not objectively well founded, refugee status cannot be granted.
propositions.quote: a conclusion that a claimant's subjective fear is not objectively well founded is fatal to the determination of Convention refugee status.

paragraphs.summary: The court states both subjective and objective components are needed under section 96, and lack of objective foundation for fear is fatal to refugee status.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellants did not show Congolese authorities had particular interest in them.
propositions.quote: The RPD was of the opinion that the appellants had not established that the Congolese authorities had a particular interest in them.

propositions.text: The RPD considered appellants' family and social situation and found crime risk was only a mere possibility.
propositions.quote: the RPD took into consideration their family and social situation and concluded that they had not established that the overall crime rate in the DRC would make the risk of a sexual or other type of assault more than a mere possibility for them.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no particular interest by authorities and crime risk was only a mere possibility for appellants.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD did not consider all evidence.
propositions.quote: The appellants submit that the RPD did not take all of the evidence into consideration.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD failed to consider all evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD considered all required elements and properly assessed and weighed all evidence.
propositions.quote: Having conducted an independent analysis, I conclude that the RPD considered all the required elements. In addition, I am of the opinion that it properly assessed and weighed all of the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD considered all required elements and properly weighed the evidence.

propositions.text: The appellants have not met their burden of proof on appeal.
propositions.quote: Consequently, I am of the opinion that the appellants have not discharged their burden of proof on appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellants failed to meet their burden of proof on appeal.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed and the RPD's decision is confirmed under paragraph 111(1)(a) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(a) of the IRPA, I dismiss the appeal and confirm the RPD's determination.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's decision under IRPA paragraph 111(1)(a).
